source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, Front Suspension, p.3-5

procedures.title: Caster and camber: adjust
parts: upper control arm inner support shaft
steps: Loosen the nuts holding the upper control arm support shaft to the crossmember.
For caster: move shims between the front and rear bolts. Moving shims from the rear bolt to the front bolt reduces positive caster.
For camber: add or remove shims equally at the front and rear bolts. Adding equal shims at both reduces positive camber.

specs.what: caster change per 1/32" shim moved from rear to front bolt
camber change per 1/32" shim at each bolt (Corvette)

notes: Shims sit between the upper control arm inner support shaft and the frame-mounted support bracket (see figure 6 in the manual).
Caster and camber can be set in the same operation.
Caster and camber specifications are in the Specifications section of the manual.

procedures.title: Steering axis inclination: check
steps: Measure steering axis inclination; if it is outside limits with camber correct, the knuckle is bent: replace it.
After fitting a new knuckle, readjust caster, camber and toe-in.
notes: Camber is the outward tilt of the wheel; steering axis inclination is the inward tilt of the knuckle. Changing one changes the other.
Specifications are given at the end of the section/book.

procedures.title: Toe-in: adjust
notes: Toe-in is the difference between the distance across the front of the two front tires and across the rear, with wheels straight ahead. Specifications are in the Specifications section.
Adjust toe-in only after caster and camber are set.
